Main.sentence: Alan Lee Keyes (born August 7, 1950) is an American politician, political scientist, and ___E:perennial candidate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perennial_candidate)___ who served as the ___E:Assistant Secretary of State for International Organization Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_Secretary_of_State_for_International_Organization_Affairs)___ from 1985 to 1987. A member of the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ , Keyes sought the nomination for ___E:President of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ in ___E:1996 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_United_States_presidential_election)___ , ___E:2000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election)___ , and ___E:2008 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

A doctoral graduate of ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ , Keyes began his diplomatic career in the ___E:U.S. Foreign Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Foreign_Service)___ in 1979 at the United States consulate in ___E:Mumbai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai)___ , India, and later in the American embassy in ___E:Zimbabwe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe)___ .

Keyes was appointed Ambassador to the ___E:Economic and Social Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Economic_and_Social_Council)___ of the United Nations by President ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ and later as President Reagan's Assistant Secretary of State for International Organization Affairs, a position he held from November 13, 1985, until November 17, 1987; in his capacities as a U.N ambassador, Keyes was involved in the implementation of the ___E:Mexico City Policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City_Policy)___ .

Aside from his presidential runs, he was the Republican nominee for the ___E:U.S. Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate)___ in Maryland against ___E:Paul Sarbanes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sarbanes)___ in ___E:1988 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_United_States_Senate_election_in_Maryland)___ and ___E:Barbara Mikulski U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Mikulski)___ in ___E:1992 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_Senate_election_in_Maryland)___ , as well as in ___E:Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois)___ against ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ in ___E:2004 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_Senate_election_in_Illinois)___ .
Keyes lost all three elections by wide margins.
Keyes hosted a radio call-in show, The Alan Keyes Show: America's Wake-Up Call , from 1994 until 1998 on ___E:WCBM U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCBM)___ .
The show was briefly simulcast by ___E:National Empowerment Television U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Empowerment_Television)___ .
In 2002, he briefly hosted a television commentary show on the ___E:MSNBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSNBC)___ cable network, Alan Keyes Is Making Sense .
He is a long time columnist for World Net Daily .

Born at the St. Albans Naval Hospital (now a ___E:VA Community Living Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Veterans_Affairs_medical_facilities_by_state#New_York)___ ) in ___E:St. Albans, Queens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Albans,_Queens)___ ,  Keyes is the fifth child of mother Gerthina (Quick) and father Allison L. Keyes, a ___E:U.S. Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)___ ___E:sergeant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergeant)___ and a teacher.
Due to his father's tours of duty, the Keyes family traveled frequently.

Keyes lived in ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ , ___E:Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland)___ , ___E:New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey)___ , New York, ___E:Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas)___ , ___E:Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia)___ and overseas in Italy.

After high school, Keyes attended ___E:Cornell University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_University)___ , where he was a member of the ___E:Cornell University Glee Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_University_Glee_Club)___ and ___E:The Hangovers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_Hangovers)___ .

He studied political philosophy with American philosopher and essayist ___E:Allan Bloom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allan_Bloom)___ and has said that Bloom was the professor who influenced him most in his undergraduate studies.
Keyes has stated that he received death threats for opposing Vietnam war protesters who seized a campus building.

Keyes has stated that a passage of Bloom's book, The Closing of the American Mind , refers to this incident,  speaking of an African-American student "whose life had been threatened by a black faculty member when the student refused to participate in a demonstration" at Cornell.
Shortly after this incident occurred, Keyes left Cornell and spent a year in Paris under a Cornell study-abroad program connected with Bloom.

Keyes continued his studies at ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ , where he resided in ___E:Winthrop House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winthrop_House)___ .
Keyes completed his Bachelor of Arts degree in government in 1972, graduating magna cum laude.
During his first year of graduate school, Keyes's roommate was ___E:William Kristol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Kristol)___ .
In 1988, Kristol ran Keyes's unsuccessful U.S.
Senate campaign in Maryland.

Keyes earned his Ph.D. in government from Harvard in 1979, having written a dissertation on ___E:Alexander Hamilton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Hamilton)___ and constitutional theory under ___E:Harvey C. Mansfield U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_C._Mansfield)___ .
Due to student deferments and a high draft number, Keyes was not drafted to serve in the ___E:Vietnam War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War)___ .

Keyes and his family were staunch supporters of the war, in which his father served two tours of duty.  Keyes was criticized by opponents of the war in Vietnam, but he says he was supporting his father and his brothers, who were also fighting in the war.

A year before completing his doctoral studies, Keyes joined the ___E:United States Department of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State)___ as a protégé of ___E:Jeane Kirkpatrick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeane_Kirkpatrick)___ .
In 1979, he was assigned to the consulate in ___E:Mumbai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai)___ , India.
The following year, Keyes was sent to serve at the embassy in ___E:Zimbabwe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe)___ .

In 1983, President ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ appointed Keyes as Ambassador to the ___E:United Nations Economic and Social Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Economic_and_Social_Council)___ .

In 1985, he was appointed ___E:Assistant Secretary of State for International Organizations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State)___ , a position he held until 1987. His stay at the UN provoked some controversy, leading Newsday to say "he has propounded the more unpopular aspects of US policy with all the diplomatic subtlety of the cannon burst in ___E:Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1812_Overture)___ ."  He also served on the staff of the ___E:National Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Security_Council)___ .

At a fundraiser for Keyes's senate campaign, President Reagan spoke of Keyes's time as an ambassador, saying that he "did such an extraordinary job ... defending our country against the forces of anti-Americanism." Reagan continued, "I've never known a more stout-hearted defender of a strong America than Alan Keyes."  In 1987 Keyes was appointed a resident scholar for the ___E:American Enterprise Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Enterprise_Institute)___ .
His principal research for ___E:AEI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Enterprise_Institute)___ was diplomacy, international relations, and self-government.

Following government service, Ambassador Keyes was President of ___E:Citizens Against Government Waste U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizens_Against_Government_Waste)___ (CAGW) from 1989 to 1991, and founded CAGW's National Taxpayers' Action Day. In 1991, he served as Interim President of ___E:Alabama A&M University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_A%26M_University)___ , in ___E:Huntsville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntsville,_Alabama)___ , Alabama.

Among the U.S. delegation to the 1984 ___E:World Population Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Population_Conference)___ in Mexico City, Keyes was selected by Reagan as deputy chairman.

In that capacity, Keyes negotiated the language of the ___E:Mexico City Policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City_Policy)___ to withhold federal funds from international organizations that support abortion.
Additionally, Keyes fought against an Arab-backed UN resolution calling for investigation of Israeli settlements.

The measure passed, 83–2, with 15 abstentions and only Israel and the U.S. voting against it.  Reagan again appointed Keyes to represent the U.S. at the 1985 Women's Conference in ___E:Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi)___ .

During his time at the ___E:United States Department of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State)___ , Keyes defended the Reagan policy of not imposing economic sanctions on South Africa as punishment for ___E:apartheid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid)___ , claiming that comprehensive ___E:U.N. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ sanctions could result in the loss of 2 million jobs for Black South Africans.

In 1988, Keyes was drafted by the Maryland Republican Party to run for the ___E:United States Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ , and received 38 percent of the vote against victorious incumbent ___E:Democrat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ ___E:Paul Sarbanes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sarbanes)___ .
Four years later, he ran again for the Senate from Maryland, coming in first in a field of 13 candidates in the Republican primary.
Against Democrat ___E:Barbara Mikulski U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Mikulski)___ , he received 29 percent in the general election.
During the 1992 election, Keyes attracted controversy when he took an $8,463 (~$16,937 in 2024)/month salary from his campaign fund.
Keyes sought the Republican presidential nomination in 1996.  In public debates, he asked other candidates about abortion.
Many Republican leaders saw this as unnecessary and divisive.

Keyes was particularly critical of Clinton during his campaign, saying, "This guy lies, but he lies with passion." He questioned whether a Republican candidate who is truthful, yet cold and heartless, had a chance to win against the incumbent.

Keyes was especially critical of ___E:Pat Buchanan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Buchanan)___ , once saying during an interview on the Talk from the Heart program with ___E:Al Kresta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Kresta)___ that Buchanan had a "black heart." [full citation needed]

Keyes's entry into the Republican race after Buchanan had secured victories in New Hampshire and Louisiana led many to believe that Keyes was a ___E:stalking horse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stalking_horse)___ for ___E:neoconservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoconservative)___ elements in the Republican Party, since Buchanan was well known as ardent foe of abortion and had suffered political fallout for bringing abortion and "cultural war" to the center of public policy debates.
Later during the primaries, Keyes was briefly detained by Atlanta police when he tried to force his way into a debate to which he had been invited, and then uninvited.
He was never formally arrested and was eventually picked up 20 minutes later by Atlanta's mayor at the time, ___E:Bill Campbell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Campbell_(mayor))___ .

Keyes again campaigned for the Republican nomination in the ___E:2000 primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States)_presidential_primaries,_2000)___ on an ___E:anti-abortion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-abortion)___ , ___E:family values U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_values)___ , tax reform plank.
In Iowa, he finished 3rd, drawing 14 percent  in a crowded field.

He stayed in the race after the early rounds and debated the two remaining candidates, ___E:John McCain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain)___ and ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ , in a number of nationally televised debates.
He finished second in 8 primaries.

His best showing in the presidential primaries was in ___E:Utah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah)___ , where he received 20 percent of the vote.  He was also noted for jumping into a ___E:mosh pit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moshing)___ during a ___E:Rage Against the Machine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rage_Against_the_Machine)___ song during the ___E:Iowa caucus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_caucus)___ as part of a segment on ___E:Michael Moore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Moore)___ 's TV series The Awful Truth .

On August 8, 2004—with 86 days to go before the general election—the Illinois Republican Party drafted Alan Keyes to run against Democratic ___E:state senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Senate)___ ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ for the U.S.

Senate, after the Republican nominee, ___E:Jack Ryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Ryan_(Senate_candidate))___ , withdrew due to a ___E:sex scandal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_scandal)___ , and other potential draftees (most notably former Illinois governor ___E:Jim Edgar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Edgar)___ and former ___E:Chicago Bears U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears)___ coach ___E:Mike Ditka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Ditka)___ ) declined to run. The Washington Post'' called Keyes a " ___E:carpetbagger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpetbagger)___ "  since he "had never lived in Illinois."   When asked to answer charges of carpetbagging in the context of his earlier criticism of ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ , he called her campaign "pure and planned selfish ambition", but stated that in his case he felt a moral obligation to run after being asked to by the Illinois Republican Party. "You are doing what you believe to be required by your respect for God's will, and I think that that's what I'm doing in Illinois".

Keyes, who opposes abortion in all cases "except as an inadvertent result of efforts to save the mother's life",  said in a September 7, 2004 news conference that Jesus Christ would not vote for Obama   because of votes that Obama—then a member of the ___E:Illinois Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Senate)___ Judiciary committee and a lecturer in ___E:constitutional law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_law)___ at the ___E:University of Chicago Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Law_School)___ —cast in 2001 against a package of three anti-abortion bills that Obama argued were too broad and unconstitutional.

The legislation, which provided "that a live child born as a result of an abortion shall be fully recognized as a human person,"  passed the Republican-controlled Illinois Senate, but failed to pass out of the Democratic-controlled ___E:Illinois House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_House_of_Representatives)___ Judiciary committee.

After the election, Keyes declined to congratulate Obama, explaining that his refusal to congratulate Obama was "not anything personal", but was meant to make a statement against "extend[ing] false congratulations to the triumph of what we have declared to be across the line" of reasonable propriety.

He said that Obama's position on moral issues regarding life and the family had crossed that line. "I'm supposed to make a call that represents the congratulations toward the triumph of that which I believe ultimately stands for ... a culture evil enough to destroy the very soul and heart of my country?
I cannot do this. And I will not make a false gesture," Keyes said.
Keyes was also criticized for his views on homosexuality.

In an interview with ___E:Michelangelo Signorile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelangelo_Signorile)___ , a gay radio host, Keyes defined homosexuality as centering in the pursuit of pleasure, literally "selfish ___E:hedonism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedonism)___ ".

When Signorile asked if ___E:Mary Cheney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Cheney)___ , Vice President ___E:Dick Cheney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Cheney)___ 's lesbian daughter, fit the description and was therefore a "selfish hedonist", Keyes replied, "Of course she is. That goes by definition."  Media sources picked up on the exchange, reporting that Keyes had "trashed", "attacked," and "lashed out at" Mary Cheney, and had called her a "sinner"—provoking condemnation of Keyes by ___E:LGBT Republicans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_Republicans)___ and several GOP leaders.

Keyes noted that it was an interviewer, not he, who brought up Mary Cheney's name in the above incident, and he told reporters, "You have tried to personalize the discussion of an issue that I did not personalize.
The people asking me the question did so, and if that's inappropriate, blame the media.
Do not blame me."
During the campaign, Keyes outlined an alternative to ___E:reparations for slavery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reparations_for_slavery)___ .

His specific suggestion was that, for a period of one or two generations, African-Americans who were descended from slaves would be exempt from the ___E:federal income tax U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_tax_in_the_United_States)___ (though not from the ___E:FICA tax U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Insurance_Contributions_Act_tax)___ that supports ___E:Social Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States))___ ).

Keyes said the experiment "would become a demonstration project for what I believe needs to be done for the whole country, which is to get rid of the income tax."  He also called for the repeal of the ___E:17th Amendment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ in order to require that U.S. senators be appointed by state legislatures, rather than being directly elected.
Keyes finished with 27% of the vote  and won a small number of southern Illinois counties.

On June 5, 2007, We Need Alan Keyes for President was formed as a ___E:political action committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_action_committee)___ to encourage Keyes to enter the 2008 presidential election.
On September 14, 2007, Keyes officially announced his candidacy in an interview with radio show host ___E:Janet Parshall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Parshall)___ .

On September 17, 2007, Keyes participated in the Values Voter Debate ___E:streamed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_video)___ live on ___E:Sky Angel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_Angel)___ , the Values Voter website, and radio.

In a ___E:straw poll U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straw_poll)___ of the attending audience, Keyes placed third among the invited candidates, after ___E:Mike Huckabee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Huckabee)___ and ___E:Ron Paul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul)___ .

Keyes was excluded from the Republican ___E:CNN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN)___ /YouTube debate on November 28, 2007. Keyes's campaign called the exclusion "arbitrary, unfair, and presumptuous," arguing that CNN was playing the role of "gatekeeper" for the presidential election.

On December 12, 2007, Keyes participated in the Des Moines Register ' s Republican presidential debate, televised nationwide by ___E:PBS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Broadcasting_Service)___ and the ___E:cable news U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_news)___ networks.
This was the first major presidential debate in which Keyes participated during the 2008 election season and the last Republican debate before the Iowa Caucuses.
Although Keyes was not listed on the latest national CNN poll leading up to the debate,  he registered with at least 1 percent of the Iowa vote in order to participate.
During the debate, after the moderator began to ask a question of Texas Congressman Ron Paul, Keyes insisted he was not getting fair treatment.

He interrupted the debate moderator at one point, saying that she had not called on him in several rounds and that he had to make an issue of it.  He went on the offensive against his opponents during the debate, criticizing ___E:Rudy Giuliani U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy_Giuliani)___ 's ___E:pro-abortion rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion-rights_movements)___ position, as well as ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ 's recent change in position on the same subject.

In answering a question about ___E:global warming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming)___ , he continued his criticisms of other candidates, saying, "I'm in favor of reducing global warming, because I think the most important emission we need to control is the hot air emission of politicians who pretend one thing and don't deliver".
He also advocated ending the income tax, establishing ___E:state-sanctioned prayer in public schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_prayer)___ , and abolishing abortion.
Toward the end of the debate, Keyes stated he could not support Giuliani if he were to win the nomination due to the former New York mayor's position on abortion.
In the ___E:Iowa caucuses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_Republican_caucuses,_2008)___ , Keyes did not appear on any of the election totals.
Keyes stated that many of the caucus locations he visited did not list him as a choice.

His campaign CEO, Stephen Stone blamed much of this on the media and on Keyes's decision to enter the race late. Stone explained that the media would not acknowledge Keyes's candidacy, making it difficult to run an effective campaign.
Keyes supports an ___E:amendment to the Constitution barring same-sex marriage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Marriage_Amendment)___ .

He stated he would not have gone to ___E:war in Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Iraq)___ ,  but also said that the war was justified  and defended President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ 's decision in one of his 2004 debates.
Keyes has stated that troops should stay in ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq)___ ,  but also said that he would have turned over operations to the United Nations.
However, Keyes has also stated that even while he was an ambassador there he was not a supporter of the United Nations.
After the early states, Keyes exclusively campaigned in ___E:Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Republican_primary,_2008)___ ,  where he finished with 0.60 percent of all votes cast.

Following Texas, the Keyes campaign moved to seeking the ___E:Constitution Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_Party_(United_States))___ presidential nomination,  but he continued to appear on several Republican ballots.
On May 6, Keyes scored his best showing of the campaign by winning 2.7% for fourth place in North Carolina, earning him two delegates to the Republican National Convention.

Keyes first stated that he was considering leaving the Republican Party during a January 2008 appearance on ___E:The Weekly Filibuster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weekly_Filibuster)___ radio show.  He did not withdraw his candidacy after ___E:John McCain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain)___ won the necessary 1,191 ___E:delegates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delegate_(American_politics))___ to the ___E:Republican National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Republican_National_Convention)___ , even though he was no longer campaigning for the Republican nomination.
On March 27, 2008, Keyes's campaign website began displaying the Constitution Party's logo, along with a parody of the trademarked GOP logo in the form of a dead elephant.
This appeared to be an indication of Keyes's intentions to quit the Republican party and to begin officially seeking the Constitution Party's presidential nomination.
On April 15, Keyes confirmed his split from the Republican Party and his intention to explore the candidacy of the Constitution Party.

He lost his bid for the party's nomination, however, coming in second to 2004 CP vice presidential candidate ___E:Chuck Baldwin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Baldwin)___ at the party's national convention in ___E:Kansas City, Missouri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri)___ , on April 26, 2008.  During the convention, the party's founder, ___E:Howard Phillips U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Phillips_(activist))___ , gave a controversial speech in which he referred to Keyes as "the ___E:Neocon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neocon)___ candidate" who "lingered in the Republican Party until a week ago."  Following the defeat, Keyes held an interview with Mike Ferguson  in which he compared his defeat to an abortion.

Later, Keyes told a group of his supporters that he was "prayerfully considering" making a continued bid for the presidency as an ___E:independent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_(politician))___ candidate,  and asserted his refusal to endorse Baldwin's candidacy.

Keyes later split from the Constitution Party; he and his supporters then formed America's Independent Party, a faction of the ___E:American Independent Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Independent_Party)___ for his presidential candidacy.
America's Independent Party gained the affiliation of a faction of California's American Independent Party.

However, the AIP ticket, which had Brian Rohrbough, father of a victim of the ___E:Columbine High School massacre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbine_High_School_massacre)___ , of ___E:Colorado U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado)___ as its vice presidential candidate, was only on the general election ballot in California, Colorado, and Florida.
In the general election held on November 4, 2008, Keyes received 47,694 votes nationally to finish seventh.
About 86% (40,673) of the votes he received were cast in California.
Keyes has worked as a media commentator and talk show personality.

In 1994, he began hosting a ___E:syndicated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_syndication)___ ___E:radio show U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_radio)___ called The Alan Keyes Show: America's Wake-Up Call for ___E:Radio America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_America_(United_States))___ from ___E:Arlington, Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington,_Virginia)___ .

The show became simulcast on cable's ___E:National Empowerment Television U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Empowerment_Television)___ in 1997.  Keyes also helped launch various web-based organizations—notably Renew America and The Declaration Foundation.

Keyes has served on the board of advisors for the ___E:Catholic League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_League_(U.S.))___ , a non-profit, ___E:Catholic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church)___ ___E:advocacy group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advocacy_group)___ headed by ___E:William A. Donohue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_A._Donohue)___ .

In 1997, he was quoted as calling in that capacity the ___E:ABC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company)___ television show Nothing Sacred "propaganda dressed up as entertainment, the way the Nazis used to make movies.
The entertainment elite's belief that there are no moral absolutes deeply contradicts the religious view of Christianity."
In 2002, he hosted a live television commentary show, Alan Keyes Is Making Sense , on the ___E:MSNBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSNBC)___ cable news channel.
The network canceled the show in July, citing poor ratings.

The cancellation triggered a boycott led by Jewish education website Mesora.org  The show was unsympathetic to supporters of the ___E:al-Aqsa Intifadah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Aqsa_Intifadah)___ —whom Keyes frequently debated on the program—and supported the Israeli crackdown on Palestinians.
The show also featured critical discussion of homosexuality and of priests accused in the Catholic Church sex abuse scandals.

The last episode was broadcast on June 27, 2002. As a result of Keyes's strong advocacy of Israel on his MSNBC show, in July 2002 the state of Israel awarded him a special honor "in appreciation of his journalistic endeavors and his integrity in reporting" and flew him in to meet Prime Minister ___E:Ariel Sharon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_Sharon)___ .

The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial court had ruled that the state law banning same-sex marriage was not constitutional.

The court gave the Massachusetts Legislature 180 days to modify the law; after it failed to do so, Romney ordered town clerks to begin issuing marriage licenses on May 17, 2004, in compliance with the court ruling.
Commenting on the issue, Keyes asked rhetorically, "Since the legislature has not acted on the subject, you might be wondering how it is that homosexuals are being married in Massachusetts.
